mainEntity.name: Which repetitive tasks should I automate first in a one-person business?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Do not automate a process merely because it is repetitive; automate it when the process is stable, frequent, easy to verify, and connected to a meaningful business objective. Research briefs, content repurposing, draft follow-ups, link checks, and project summaries are often better starting points than complex customer decisions.

Context: Run My AI Business includes specialized assistants for these kinds of activities and recommends choosing relevant workflows, building one, using it, and expanding gradually.

Key factors:
- Frequency and volume
- Error tolerance
- Standardized inputs
- Review time compared with manual effort

Practical guidance: Write a simple operating procedure first. If people perform the task differently each time, clarify the process before adding AI; otherwise, automation may reproduce confusion faster.

The business’s bot examples can help owners identify a suitable first workflow.
acceptedAnswer.description: Start with frequent, text-heavy tasks that are easy to review, such as research collection, content repurposing, draft email follow-up, link checking, or weekly project summaries. Clarify the process first, define the required inputs, and avoid automating decisions that require nuanced judgment.
